sections.name: View
sections.description:
View constructs an empty retained container. Append content with Child or
Children and configure it with fluent properties, events, and styles.

entries.name: Child
entries.description: Child appends content and returns this element. Content can be an element, native node, scalar, accessor, or node-returning construction callback.

entries.name: Children
entries.description: Children appends multiple children in order without replacing existing content. It also accepts []any, []*Element, and []*native.Node slices as arguments. Read the retained child nodes through element.Node.Children.

entries.name: Style
entries.description: Style merges a reusable style. Scalar accessors retain independent native bindings.

go/ui/button.example:
func ButtonExample(save func()) *ui.Element {
	return ui.Button().Child("Save changes").
		Height(40).
		PaddingLeft(16).
		PaddingRight(16).
		BackgroundColor("#2563eb").
		TextColor("white").
		BorderRadius(8).
		Hover(func(s ui.StyleBuilder) ui.StyleBuilder { return s.BackgroundColor("#3b82f6") }).
		OnClick(save)

}

entries.description: Decode a supported image file synchronously with encoded and decoded size limits. Prefer passing a path to [`crate::img`] for event-driven background loading. This method is useful when an application already owns a background execution context. Paths whose stem ends in `Template`, optionally followed by a scale suffix such as `@2x`, are marked for macOS template rendering. Call [`Self::template`] to override that convention.

sections.name: Checkbox
sections.signature: pub fn new(state: impl Into<ToggleState>) -> Self

entries.name: parent
entries.type: pub fn parent(children: impl IntoIterator<Item = bool>) -> Self
entries.description: Derive a parent checkbox from the checked values of the boxes it governs. This is Base UI's `parent` checkbox: every child checked reports on, none reports off, and a mix reports mixed. QuickGUI keeps no child registry — the application passes the values it is already rendering — so the derivation stays a pure function of the caller's own data. ``` use quickgui::{Checkbox, ToggleState}; assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([true, true]).state(), ToggleState::On); assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([false, false]).state(), ToggleState::Off); assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([true, false]).state(), ToggleState::Mixed); // An empty group is unchecked rather than mixed. assert_eq!(Checkbox::parent([]).state(), ToggleState::Off); ```

entries.name: read_only
entries.type: pub const fn read_only(mut self, read_only: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Show a value the user may read but not change, Base UI's `readOnly`. Unlike a disabled checkbox, a read-only one stays focusable and stays in the Tab sequence. QuickGUI projects the state and refuses the transition through [`Self::next_state`]; the application's own listener asks for that transition rather than toggling blindly.

entries.name: state
entries.description: Configures state for this part.

entries.name: is_read_only
entries.description: Configures is read only for this part.

entries.name: next_state
entries.description: The state an activation moves this checkbox to, or `None` when it refuses. Mixed and off both move to on, and on moves to off, which is the web's tri-state contract. A read-only checkbox returns `None`, so a click listener that asks before writing cannot change a value the control is refusing.

entries.name: parent_next_checked
entries.description: The checked value activating a parent checkbox moves its whole group to. A partially or fully unchecked parent checks everything; a fully checked one clears it. Returns `None` when the parent is read-only.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::root_with
sections.signature: pub fn root_with(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned group root without adding layout or appearance. Pair it with a [`crate::Field`] label, or with [`crate::Element::accessibility_labelled_by`], to name the group.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::root
sections.description: Create the unstyled root part. Use [`Self::root_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::checkbox_with
sections.signature: pub fn checkbox_with(self, value: impl Into<ElementId>, checkbox: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one application-owned checkbox for `value`. The part reuses the existing [`Checkbox`] descriptor, so the checkbox role, exact on/off/mixed semantics, click behavior, and desktop pointer contract are identical to a standalone checkbox. A disabled group disables every item.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::checkbox

sections.description: Create the unstyled checkbox part. Use [`Self::checkbox_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.signature: pub fn indicator_with(self, indicator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Hide an application-owned indicator inside one item from the accessible name.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::indicator
sections.description: Create the unstyled indicator part. Use [`Self::indicator_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::parent_with
sections.signature: pub fn parent_with(self, parent: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned parent checkbox. Its checked state is derived: on when every declared value is checked, mixed when only some are, and off when none are. QuickGUI retains no separate parent value, so the parent can never disagree with its children.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup::parent
sections.description: Create the unstyled parent part. Use [`Self::parent_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Slider::root_with
sections.signature: pub fn root_with(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance. A single-thumb slider becomes the focusable Slider itself. Pair it with [`Self::key_with`] to attach the typed keyboard actions.

sections.name: Slider::root
sections.description: Create the unstyled root part. Use [`Self::root_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.description: Attach QuickGUI's typed slider keyboard actions to a single-thumb root. Install [`slider_key_bindings`] once on the application keymap. Multi-thumb sliders use [`SliderThumb::key_with`] instead so each thumb owns its own focus.

sections.description: Attach the typed slider keyboard actions against a per-instance state accessor.

sections.name: Slider::track_with

sections.description: Decorate an application-owned track. Base UI uses [`Self::control_with`] as the larger interactive surface. A declaration that omits Control can keep the earlier behavior by attaching a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::track_id`] and forwarding the event to [`SliderState::apply_pointer`] with the size the caller laid out.

sections.name: Slider::track

sections.name: Slider::range
sections.description: Create the unstyled range part. Use [`Self::range_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Slider::indicator_with
sections.signature: pub fn indicator_with(self, indicator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Base UI's Indicator name for the filled part of the track. This is the same decorator as [`Self::range_with`]; both names stay supported.

sections.name: Slider::indicator
sections.description: Create the unstyled indicator part. Use [`Self::indicator_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Slider::control_with
sections.signature: pub fn control_with(self, control: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned interactive area that carries the slider's pointer capture. Base UI separates the Control — the region a press acts on — from the Track it paints. Attach a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::control_id`] and forward the event to [`SliderState::apply_pointer_change`] with the size the caller laid out. A caller that omits this part can keep pointer capture on [`Self::track_with`].

sections.name: Slider::control
sections.description: Create the unstyled control part. Use [`Self::control_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Slider::label_with

sections.description: Assign the stable mounted label target the slider points at. A single-thumb slider takes its accessible name from this part. A multi-thumb slider names its group from it, and each thumb still needs its own accessible name.

sections.name: Slider::label
sections.description: Create the unstyled label part. Use [`Self::label_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Slider::value_with
sections.signature: pub fn value_with(self, value: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Assign the stable mounted value target the slider points at. Put [`Self::display_value`] inside it; QuickGUI never renders the text itself.

entries.name: offset
entries.type: pub fn offset(self, track_length: f32, thumb_length: f32) -> f32
entries.description: The leading-edge offset of this thumb along the track, honoring the thumb alignment. `track_length` and `thumb_length` are measured along the slider's own axis. sections.name: NumberField::root_with
sections.signature: pub fn root_with(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: NumberField::root
sections.description: Create the unstyled root part. Use [`Self::root_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: NumberField::input_with
sections.signature: pub fn input_with(self, state: &NumberFieldState, input: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned controlled input. Pass a [`crate::text_input`] built from [`NumberFieldState::text`] with the caller's own [`crate::Element::on_input`] listener. QuickGUI adds the spin-button semantics: the committed numeric value, the field's bounds and step, and invalid state.

sections.name: NumberField::input
sections.description: Create the unstyled input part. Use [`Self::input_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: NumberField::increment_with
sections.signature: pub fn increment_with(self, state: &NumberFieldState, increment: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned increment button. Steppers stay out of the Tab sequence because the input already answers arrow keys, which matches native desktop spin buttons.

sections.name: NumberField::increment
sections.description: Create the unstyled increment part. Use [`Self::increment_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: NumberField::decrement_with
sections.signature: pub fn decrement_with(self, state: &NumberFieldState, decrement: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned decrement button.

sections.name: NumberField::decrement
sections.description: Create the unstyled decrement part. Use [`Self::decrement_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: NumberField::group_with
sections.signature: pub fn group_with(self, group: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned group that wraps the decrement, input, and increment parts. Base UI's Group keeps the three controls one addressable unit; QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the Group role and adds no layout, so the application still chooses the row, the order, and the spacing.

sections.name: NumberField::group
sections.description: Create the unstyled group part. Use [`Self::group_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: NumberField::scrub_area_with
sections.signature: pub fn scrub_area_with(self, state: &NumberFieldState, scrub_area: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned area a pointer drag scrubs the value over. Attach a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::scrub_area_id`] and forward the event to [`NumberFieldState::apply_scrub`]. QuickGUI supplies the identity, the axis-appropriate resize cursor, drag exclusion, and text-selection suppression; the area is hidden from assistive technology because the input already carries the spin-button semantics.

sections.name: NumberField::scrub_area
sections.description: Create the unstyled scrub area part. Use [`Self::scrub_area_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: NumberField::scrub_area_cursor_with
sections.signature: pub fn scrub_area_cursor_with(self, cursor: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned cursor a scrub area shows while it is being dragged. Mount it only while [`NumberFieldState::is_scrubbing`] is true and place it from [`NumberFieldState::scrub_position`]; QuickGUI supplies the identity and keeps the decoration out of the accessible name and out of hit testing.

sections.name: NumberField::scrub_area_cursor
sections.description: Create the unstyled scrub area cursor part. Use [`Self::scrub_area_cursor_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: SelectState::element
sections.signature: pub fn element<V, PopoverRoot, RenderOption, Change>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, label: impl Into<Arc<str>>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut SelectState<T>, trigger: Element, popover_root: PopoverRoot, render_option: RenderOption, change: Change, ) -> Element where V: 'static, T: Clone + 'static, PopoverRoot: Fn(SelectListState) -> Element + Clone + 'static, RenderOption: Fn(&PickerItem<T>, SelectOptionState) -> Element + Clone + 'static, Change: Fn(&mut V, T, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,

This is the `fn`-pointer entry point: a view that owns one select per field passes `Self::field`. A host that renders many declared selects through one view passes a per-instance [`StateAccessor`] to [`SelectState::element_with`] instead.

sections.description: Build the select interaction against a per-instance retained-state accessor. Two selects declared by one view stay independent because the accessor, not the view type, decides which [`SelectState`] each registered listener resolves.

The surface renderer additionally receives [`SelectPopupParts`], whose `scroll_up_arrow_with` and `scroll_down_arrow_with` decorators carry Base UI's hovered scrolling behavior. <Field.Root required invalid={name().length === 0} validationMessage="Enter a name">
  <Field.Label><Text>Name</Text></Field.Label>
  <Field.Control value={name()} onInput={(event) => setName(event.value ?? "")} />
  <Field.Description><Text>Shown on your profile.</Text></Field.Description>
  <Field.Error><Text>Enter a name.</Text></Field.Error>
</Field.Root>

entries.name: validation_debounce
entries.type: pub fn validation_debounce(mut self, debounce: Duration) -> Self
entries.description: Wait this long after a change before revalidating, Base UI's `validationDebounceTime`. The interval is an exact one-shot deadline the application schedules with [`crate::AsyncViewContext::sleep`]; QuickGUI never polls, and a field that is not being typed into owns nothing. It applies to [`FieldValidationTrigger::Change`] only — a blur or a submit is a deliberate boundary and validates immediately. Clamped to [`MAX_FIELD_VALIDATION_DEBOUNCE`].

entries.name: should_validate
entries.type: pub const fn should_validate(&self, trigger: FieldValidationTrigger) -> bool
entries.description: Whether the declared mode expects this event to recompute validity. A submit always validates; a blur validates on `OnBlur` and `OnChange`; a change validates only on `OnChange`.

entries.name: validation_delay
entries.type: pub const fn validation_delay(&self, trigger: FieldValidationTrigger) -> Option<Duration>
entries.description: How long to wait before recomputing validity for this event, when it validates at all. Returns `None` when the declared mode ignores the event, and `Some(Duration::ZERO)` when it validates immediately, so a listener can branch once instead of re-deriving the policy.

sections.name: Field::validity_with
sections.signature: pub fn validity_with(&self, visible: bool, validity: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned part that is shown only for a chosen validity, Base UI's Field.Validity. `visible` is the application's own predicate over [`Self::state`] — "invalid and touched", "valid and dirty", whatever the product means. QuickGUI removes the part from layout, paint, input, and the accessibility tree when the predicate is false, exactly as [`Self::error_with`] does, so an unmatched validity costs nothing.

sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance. The root is the group that names the whole code and carries its validity, so assistive technology announces one field rather than a row of unrelated one-character inputs.

sections.name: OtpField::root

sections.name: OtpField::input_with

sections.description: Decorate one application-owned slot input without adding appearance. Pass a [`crate::text_input`] built from [`OtpFieldState::slot_text`]. sections.name: Element
sections.description: Every part returns a fluent element. Strings, numbers, elements, and deferred child factories compose directly.

entries.name: Child
entries.description:
Child appends content and returns this element. Content can be an element,
native node, scalar, accessor, or node-returning construction callback.

entries.name: Children
entries.description:
Children appends multiple children in order without replacing existing content.
It also accepts []any, []*Element, and []*native.Node slices as arguments.
Read the retained child nodes through element.Node.Children.

entries.name: Style

Style merges a reusable style. Scalar
accessors retain independent native bindings.

sections.description: Decorate an application-owned root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: ScrollArea::root
sections.description: Create the unstyled root part. Use [`Self::root_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: ScrollArea::viewport_with
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_with(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned scroll container. The viewport clips its content on both axes and carries the ScrollView role. The caller places the content by translating [`Self::content_with`] with the retained offset, which keeps scrolling paint-only and keeps QuickGUI's built-in overlay scrollbar out of a component whose scrollbars the application draws itself.

sections.name: ScrollArea::viewport
sections.description: Create the unstyled viewport part. Use [`Self::viewport_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: ScrollArea::content_with
sections.signature: pub fn content_with(self, content: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned scrolled content. Translate it by the negated [`ScrollAreaState::offset`]; QuickGUI adds no transform of its own so the application keeps full control of the motion.

sections.name: ScrollArea::content
sections.description: Create the unstyled content part. Use [`Self::content_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: ScrollArea::scrollbar_with
sections.signature: pub fn scrollbar_with( self, state: &ScrollAreaState, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation, scrollbar: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one application-owned scrollbar track. The track projects the ScrollBar role with the exact current position, the scrollable range, and its orientation. It is not focusable: a scrollbar duplicates keyboard scrolling the viewport already provides, so it stays out of the Tab sequence.

sections.name: ScrollArea::scrollbar
sections.signature: pub fn scrollbar(self, state: &ScrollAreaState, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation) -> Element
sections.description: Create the unstyled scrollbar part. Use [`Self::scrollbar_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: ScrollArea::thumb_with
sections.signature: pub fn thumb_with(self, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation, thumb: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one application-owned scrollbar thumb. The thumb carries the captured pointer drag. Attach a [`crate::ViewContext::pointer_listener`] registered for [`Self::thumb_id`] and forward the event to [`ScrollAreaState::apply_thumb_pointer`] with the track length the caller laid out.

sections.name: ScrollArea::thumb
sections.signature: pub fn thumb(self, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation) -> Element
sections.description: Create the unstyled thumb part. Use [`Self::thumb_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: ScrollArea::positioned_thumb_with
sections.signature: pub fn positioned_thumb_with( self, state: &ScrollAreaState, orientation: ScrollAreaOrientation, track_length: f32, thumb: Element, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate and position one application-owned scrollbar thumb inside its scrollbar. This is [`Self::thumb_with`] plus the structural geometry a draggable thumb needs: the thumb is absolutely positioned along the scrollbar's axis at [`ScrollAreaState::thumb_offset`] with [`ScrollAreaState::thumb_length`], so it follows the offset without the application re-deriving either value. Cross-axis size and every visual property stay application-owned.

sections.name: TableState::element
sections.signature: pub fn element<V, H, E, RenderHeader, RenderCell, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, columns: &[TableColumn], access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut TableState, render_header: RenderHeader, render_cell: RenderCell, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, H: IntoElement, E: IntoElement, RenderHeader: FnMut(TableHeaderState<'_>) -> H, RenderCell: FnMut(TableCellState<'_>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, TableCellPosition, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build a complete unstyled virtualized, sortable, keyboard-navigable table. `render_header` owns every visible header declaration, including label, sort indicator, and the placement of the resize handle QuickGUI hands it. `render_cell` owns every visible cell declaration, including the inline editor it mounts while `editing` is set, and runs only for mounted rows. QuickGUI decorates those elements with fixed grid geometry, identities, pointer/keyboard behavior, and accessibility semantics but adds no paint. `activate` receives the current logical cell when Return is dispatched outside an editor; selection, sort, width, order, and editing state remain directly readable from `access`.

sections.name: TableState::element_with
sections.signature: pub fn element_with<V, H, E, RenderHeader, RenderCell, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, columns: &[TableColumn], access_source: StateAccessor<V, TableState>, render_header: RenderHeader, render_cell: RenderCell, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, H: IntoElement, E: IntoElement, RenderHeader: FnMut(TableHeaderState<'_>) -> H, RenderCell: FnMut(TableCellState<'_>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, TableCellPosition, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build the table against a per-instance retained-state accessor. A host that renders many declared tables through one view passes an accessor that captures which [`TableState`] each registered listener resolves. Every row is a plain container; [`Self::element_with_rows`] lets the caller paint the rows too.

sections.name: TableState::element_with_rows
sections.signature: pub fn element_with_rows<V, R, H, E, RenderRow, RenderHeader, RenderCell, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, columns: &[TableColumn], access_source: StateAccessor<V, TableState>, mut render_row: RenderRow, mut render_header: RenderHeader, mut render_cell: RenderCell, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, R: IntoElement, H: IntoElement, E: IntoElement, RenderRow: FnMut(TableRowState) -> R, RenderHeader: FnMut(TableHeaderState<'_>) -> H, RenderCell: FnMut(TableCellState<'_>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, TableCellPosition, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build the table with a caller-owned container for every mounted row. `render_row` returns the element a row's cells are laid out in. QuickGUI adds the grid tracks, the row height, the row identity, and the collection semantics on top of it, so the caller declares only the row's paint — a background, a divider, a hover state, or a [`selected_style`](Element::selected_style) that paints while the row is selected — never its layout. The renderer runs only for mounted rows.

entries.description: Supply the children of a pending branch in one atomic, validated splice. The replacement is built and validated before any live state changes: an over-deep, oversize, or duplicate-ID payload leaves the tree exactly as it was. On success the branch stops being pending, its placeholder row disappears, and selection, expansion, and the logical scroll anchor are preserved. An unknown node ID reports `Ok(false)`.

sections.name: TreeState::element
sections.signature: pub fn element<V, E, RenderRow, Activate>( &mut self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut TreeState<T>, render_row: RenderRow, activate: Activate, ) -> Element where V: 'static, T: 'static, E: IntoElement, RenderRow: FnMut(TreeRow<'_, T>, Option<Element>) -> E, Activate: Fn(&mut V, ElementId, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build a complete unstyled virtualized, expandable, keyboard-navigable tree. `render_row` runs only for mounted rows and receives an optional behavior-decorated, appearance-free disclosure element. The caller decides where to place that control and owns the complete row layout and paint. QuickGUI decorates the returned row with fixed virtual geometry, tree semantics, selection, and pointer behavior. `activate` receives the selected application value by stable node ID; the tree retains no closure or scheduler afterward.

entries.name: apply_loading_status
entries.type: pub fn apply_loading_status<V: 'static>( view: &mut V, cx: &mut EventContext, access: &StateAccessor<V, AvatarState>, status: AvatarLoadingStatus, now: Instant, on_loading_status_change: impl FnOnce(&mut V, AvatarLoadingStatus, &mut EventContext), ) -> bool
entries.description: Apply a load status reported by the application and notify the owner exactly once. QuickGUI decodes images on a worker pool without a per-element completion event, so the application reports the status it already knows — from its own `cx.spawn` load, an [`crate::ImageResource`] loader, or a hosted renderer — and this is the `onLoadingStatusChange` counterpart: the retained status changes, the exact fallback deadline is re-armed, and `on_loading_status_change` runs only for a real transition. Returns whether the retained state changed.

entries.description: Ask for the one repaint an armed fallback deadline needs. Call this while rendering. A settled avatar requests nothing, so the window stays asleep.

entries.description: Give this indicator a stable identity so its label and value parts can be related to it. sections.name: Meter
sections.signature: pub fn new(value: f64, minimum: f64, maximum: f64) -> Self
sections.description: Create a meter. Non-finite bounds fall back to `0.0..=1.0` and an inverted range is swapped.

entries.name: low

entries.description: Mark the upper end of the low range. Values outside the meter bounds are clamped.

entries.description: Mark the lower end of the high range.

entries.name: optimum

entries.description: Mark the most favorable value inside the range.

entries.description: Give this meter a stable identity so its label and value parts can be related to it.

sections.description: Every part returns a fluent element. Strings, numbers, elements, and deferred child factories compose directly.

entries.name: Child
entries.description:
Child appends content and returns this element. Content can be an element,
native node, scalar, accessor, or node-returning construction callback.

entries.name: Children
entries.description:
Children appends multiple children in order without replacing existing content.
It also accepts []any, []*Element, and []*native.Node slices as arguments.
Read the retained child nodes through element.Node.Children.

entries.name: Style
entries.description:
Style merges a reusable style. Scalar
accessors retain independent native bindings.

typescript/ui/toolbar.example:
<Toolbar.Root
  items={[{ value: "back" }, { value: "forward" }, { value: "search" }]}
  active={active()}
  onActiveChange={setActive}
>
  <Toolbar.Button partValue="back"><Text>Back</Text></Toolbar.Button>
  <Toolbar.Button partValue="forward"><Text>Forward</Text></Toolbar.Button>
  <Toolbar.Input partValue="search" placeholder="Search" />
</Toolbar.Root>

sections.name: Toolbar::root_with
sections.signature: pub fn root_with(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned toolbar root without adding layout or appearance.

sections.name: Toolbar::root
sections.description: Create the unstyled root part. Use [`Self::root_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Toolbar::group_with
sections.signature: pub fn group_with(self, group: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned group of related toolbar items, Base UI's Toolbar.Group. The group is a labelling and structural unit only: every item inside it keeps taking part in the toolbar's single roving Tab stop, so grouping never creates a second focus scope.

sections.name: Toolbar::group
sections.description: Create the unstyled group part. Use [`Self::group_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Toolbar::separator_with
sections.signature: pub fn separator_with(self, separator: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned divider between toolbar groups, Base UI's Toolbar.Separator. A separator carries the Separator role across the toolbar's cross axis and never takes focus, so arrow navigation steps straight past it.

sections.name: Toolbar::separator
sections.description: Create the unstyled separator part. Use [`Self::separator_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Popover
sections.signature: pub fn new( trigger_id: impl Into<ElementId>, surface_id: impl Into<ElementId>, open: bool, ) -> Self

entries.name: open
entries.type: pub const fn open(mut self, open: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Replace the controlled open flag, Base UI's Root `open` prop. The descriptor is copied per frame, so a component that retains the open flag itself can build one descriptor at construction time and stamp the current value onto it here.

entries.name: kind
entries.type: pub const fn kind(mut self, kind: PopoverKind) -> Self
entries.description: Configures kind for this part.

entries.name: placement
entries.type: pub const fn placement(mut self, placement: AnchorPlacement) -> Self
entries.description: Configures placement for this part.

entries.name: side
entries.type: pub const fn side(self, side: AnchorSide) -> Self
entries.description: Prefer one side of the anchor, keeping the current cross-axis alignment. This is the side half of [`Self::placement`], matching Base UI's `side` prop. A side is a preference: QuickGUI flips to the opposite side when the preferred one does not fit, and [`Self::resolved_side`] reports what actually happened.

entries.name: align
entries.type: pub const fn align(self, align: AnchorAlign) -> Self
entries.description: Prefer a cross-axis alignment, keeping the current side. This is the alignment half of [`Self::placement`], matching Base UI's `align` prop.

entries.name: side_offset
entries.type: pub fn side_offset(self, offset: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the distance between the anchor and the positioner, Base UI's `sideOffset`. This is the Base UI-named alias of [`Self::anchor_gap`]. Both names stay supported and write the same bounded value.

entries.name: align_offset
entries.type: pub fn align_offset(mut self, offset: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Shift the popover along its cross axis before collision handling, Base UI's `alignOffset`. Positive values move right on a top or bottom placement and down on a left or right placement. The shift runs before the surface is clamped into the viewport, so it can slide a popup along its trigger but never push it off screen.

entries.name: collision_padding
entries.type: pub fn collision_padding(self, padding: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the collision padding kept inside the window viewport, Base UI's `collisionPadding`. This is the Base UI-named alias of [`Self::viewport_margin`]. Both names stay supported.

entries.name: sticky
entries.type: pub const fn sticky(mut self, sticky: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Choose whether the popover is kept inside the collision viewport, Base UI's `sticky`. QuickGUI keeps anchored surfaces on screen by default, which is Base UI's sticky behavior. Passing `false` locks the popover to its anchor so it travels off screen with a scrolling row instead of detaching from it.

entries.name: anchor_element
entries.type: pub fn anchor_element(mut self, anchor: impl Into<ElementId>) -> Self
entries.description: Position against a different mounted element instead of the trigger, Base UI's `anchor`.

entries.name: anchor_point
entries.type: pub fn anchor_point(mut self, anchor: Point) -> Self
entries.description: Position against a logical window point instead of the trigger, Base UI's virtual `anchor`.

entries.name: anchor_trigger
entries.type: pub const fn anchor_trigger(mut self) -> Self
entries.description: Position against the trigger again, undoing an anchor override.

entries.name: modal
entries.type: pub const fn modal(mut self, modal: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Make the open popover modal, Base UI's `modal` prop. A modal popover contains Tab focus inside the popup and expects a mounted [`Self::backdrop_with`] to absorb outside pointer input. QuickGUI adds no dimming: the backdrop stays an invisible caller-owned element until the application paints it.

entries.name: is_modal
entries.description: Whether this popover contains focus while open.

entries.name: arrow_size
entries.type: pub fn arrow_size(mut self, size: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Declare the edge length of a framework-positioned arrow. [`Self::arrow_with`] centers an arrow of this size on the anchor. Leaving it at zero pins the arrow to the resolved edge without a cross-axis offset, which is what an application that centers the arrow with its own layout wants.

entries.name: arrow_padding
entries.type: pub fn arrow_padding(mut self, padding: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Keep a framework-positioned arrow this far from the popup's corners, Base UI's `arrowPadding`.

entries.name: track_placement
entries.type: pub fn track_placement(mut self, placement: &AnchorPlacementHandle) -> Self
entries.description: Adopt the placement QuickGUI resolved for this popover on the previous painted frame. Store an [`AnchorPlacementHandle`] on the view next to `open`, mount the positioner with [`Self::tracked_positioner_with`] or [`Self::tracked_surface_with`], and pass the handle here while declaring the next frame. [`Self::arrow_with`], [`Self::resolved_side`], [`Self::resolved_align`], and [`Self::state`] then follow the placement the popover really used instead of the declared preference. QuickGUI requests exactly one correcting frame when the resolved placement changes, so a flipped popover settles immediately and an unflipped one adds no redraw source.

entries.name: resolved_placement
entries.type: pub const fn resolved_placement(mut self, resolved: Option<ResolvedAnchorPlacement>) -> Self
entries.description: Adopt an already-read placement report. Use this when the application keeps the snapshot itself rather than the handle.

entries.name: resolved_side
entries.description: The side the popover actually opened on, or the declared preference before the first frame.

entries.name: resolved_align
entries.description: The cross-axis alignment the popover actually used, or the declared preference.

entries.name: resolved_anchor_placement
entries.description: The full placement the popover actually used, or the declared preference.

entries.name: state
entries.description: A copyable snapshot of what Base UI exposes as `data-*` attributes and CSS variables. The application styles from this: it picks a transform origin from [`PopoverPartState::side`], hides a popup whose anchor scrolled away using [`PopoverPartState::anchor_hidden`], matches the trigger width with [`PopoverPartState::anchor_width`], and caps a scrolling viewport with [`PopoverPartState::available_height`]. Every measured field stays zero until the popover has been painted once with a bound placement handle.

entries.name: anchor_gap
entries.type: pub fn anchor_gap(mut self, gap: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the structural distance between the trigger and positioner.

entries.name: viewport_margin
entries.type: pub fn viewport_margin(mut self, margin: f32) -> Self
entries.description: Set the structural collision margin inside the current window viewport.

entries.name: initial_focus
entries.type: pub fn initial_focus(mut self, focus: impl Into<ElementId>) -> Self
entries.description: Prefer a mounted popover descendant instead of the popover root when opening.

entries.name: dismiss_on_escape
entries.type: pub const fn dismiss_on_escape(mut self, dismiss: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Configures dismiss on escape for this part.

entries.name: dismiss_on_pointer_outside
entries.type: pub const fn dismiss_on_pointer_outside(mut self, dismiss: bool) -> Self
entries.description: Configures dismiss on pointer outside for this part.

entries.name: is_open
entries.description: Configures is open for this part.

entries.name: trigger_id
entries.description: Configures trigger id for this part.

entries.name: surface_id
entries.description: Stable popover identity retained under the existing `surface` name.

sections.name: Popover::positioner_with
sections.signature: pub fn positioner_with(self, positioner: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned portal/positioner without adding popover appearance. QuickGUI's retained overlay node is itself the portal, so this part combines the Base UI-style Portal and Positioner boundary without introducing a full-window wrapper that would block unrelated pointer input.

sections.name: Popover::positioner
sections.description: Create the unstyled positioner part. Use [`Self::positioner_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Popover::tracked_positioner_with
sections.signature: pub fn tracked_positioner_with( self, positioner: Element, placement: &AnchorPlacementHandle, ) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the positioner and publish the placement it resolves to. This is [`Self::positioner_with`] plus [`crate::Element::report_anchor_placement`]: the handle receives the side, alignment, anchor rectangle, and remaining room the popover actually used, and [`Self::track_placement`] feeds it back into the descriptor on the next frame.

sections.name: Popover::portal_with
sections.signature: pub fn portal_with(self, portal: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Base UI's Portal name for the combined portal/positioner part. QuickGUI's retained overlay node is itself the portal, so Portal and Positioner are one element; both names decorate it identically.

sections.name: Popover::portal

sections.name: Popover::popup_with
sections.signature: pub fn popup_with(self, popover: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an application-owned popover without adding layout or appearance. The popover emits [`crate::Event::Dismiss`] under [`Self::surface_id`] for every enabled dismissal path. Mounted title/description parts are related without copying their text.

sections.name: Popover::popup
sections.description: Create the unstyled popup part. Use [`Self::popup_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Popover::surface_with
sections.signature: pub fn surface_with(self, surface: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate one caller-owned element as both positioner and popover. This compact form has the same unstyled contract as composing [`Self::positioner_with`] around [`Self::popup_with`]. Use separate parts when the application needs to animate or size the positioner independently from popover presentation.

sections.description: Decorate the merged surface and publish the placement it resolves to.

sections.name: Popover::surface
sections.description: Create an unstyled merged positioner/popover root.

sections.name: Popover::arrow_with
sections.signature: pub fn arrow_with(self, arrow: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Position a caller-owned arrow on the edge the popover actually opened against. The arrow is absolutely positioned inside the popup, pinned to the edge that faces the anchor and centered on the anchor along the cross axis. When [`Self::track_placement`] has supplied a placement report the offsets follow the real placement, including a flip — never the declared preference. Before the first painted frame, or without a bound handle, the arrow follows the declared side and stays centered on the popup, and QuickGUI's one correcting frame moves it as soon as the real placement is known. The application owns the arrow's size, shape, rotation, and color. Declare [`Self::arrow_size`] when QuickGUI should center an arrow of a known edge length, and [`Self::arrow_padding`] to keep it clear of the popup's corners. The arrow is hidden from assistive technology: it is decoration attached to a surface that already carries the relationship.

sections.name: Popover::arrow
sections.description: Create the unstyled arrow part. Use [`Self::arrow_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Popover::viewport_with
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_with(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate a caller-owned scrolling viewport mounted inside the popup. Base UI's Viewport clips content that changes size between triggers so the popup can animate between them. QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the scroll container; height, padding, and motion stay application-owned — cap it with [`PopoverPartState::available_height`] to keep a long popup inside the window.

sections.description: Every part returns a fluent element. Strings, numbers, elements, and deferred child factories compose directly.

entries.name: Child
entries.description:
Child appends content and returns this element. Content can be an element,
native node, scalar, accessor, or node-returning construction callback.

entries.name: Children
entries.description:
Children appends multiple children in order without replacing existing content.
It also accepts []any, []*Element, and []*native.Node slices as arguments.
Read the retained child nodes through element.Node.Children.

Style merges a reusable style. Scalar
accessors retain independent native bindings.

typescript/ui/dialog.example:
<Dialog.Root open={open()} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Dialog.Trigger><Text>Edit profile</Text></Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Portal>
    <Dialog.Backdrop />
    <Dialog.Viewport>
      <Dialog.Popup>
        <Dialog.Title><Text>Edit profile</Text></Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description><Text>Changes are saved immediately.</Text></Dialog.Description>
        <Dialog.Close><Text>Done</Text></Dialog.Close>
      </Dialog.Popup>
    </Dialog.Viewport>
  </Dialog.Portal>
</Dialog.Root>

sections.name: Dialog::popup_with

sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned modal popover. The popover is a negative-Tab-index focus fallback. Enabled descendant Tab stops are chosen first when the enclosing trap mounts. Title and description relationships project only when the corresponding parts are mounted, so incomplete compositions never emit dangling native node references.

sections.name: Dialog::viewport_with
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_with(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned scrolling viewport the popup sits inside, Base UI's Viewport. A dialog taller than the window must scroll as one surface rather than clipping its own content, and the scroll must live outside the popup so the popup keeps its own padding and shadow. QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the scroll container; size, alignment, and padding stay application-owned.

typescript/ui/alert-dialog.example:
<AlertDialog.Root open={open()} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <AlertDialog.Trigger><Text>Delete project</Text></AlertDialog.Trigger>
  <AlertDialog.Portal>
    <AlertDialog.Backdrop />
    <AlertDialog.Viewport>
      <AlertDialog.Popup>
        <AlertDialog.Title><Text>Delete this project?</Text></AlertDialog.Title>
        <AlertDialog.Description><Text>This cannot be undone.</Text></AlertDialog.Description>
        <AlertDialog.Close><Text>Cancel</Text></AlertDialog.Close>
      </AlertDialog.Popup>
    </AlertDialog.Viewport>
  </AlertDialog.Portal>
</AlertDialog.Root>

sections.name: Dialog::popup_with
sections.signature: pub fn popup_with(self, popover: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned modal popover. The popover is a negative-Tab-index focus fallback. Enabled descendant Tab stops are chosen first when the enclosing trap mounts. Title and description relationships project only when the corresponding parts are mounted, so incomplete compositions never emit dangling native node references.

sections.name: Dialog::popup
sections.description: Create the unstyled popup part. Use [`Self::popup_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: Dialog::viewport_with
sections.signature: pub fn viewport_with(self, viewport: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned scrolling viewport the popup sits inside, Base UI's Viewport. A dialog taller than the window must scroll as one surface rather than clipping its own content, and the scroll must live outside the popup so the popup keeps its own padding and shadow. QuickGUI supplies the stable identity and the scroll container; size, alignment, and padding stay application-owned.

entries.name: Children

sections.signature: pub fn new( trigger_id: impl Into<ElementId>, popup_id: impl Into<ElementId>, open: bool, ) -> Self

entries.description: Configures placement for this part.

entries.description: Set the structural collision margin inside the current window viewport.

entries.name: on_trigger_hover
entries.type: pub fn on_trigger_hover<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PreviewCardState, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the trigger's hover behavior. Attach the returned handle with [`crate::Element::on_hover`]. `on_open_change` runs only when the open value actually changes, which for the delayed open is on the frame the deadline is applied rather than on the pointer event that armed it.

entries.name: on_trigger_hover_with
entries.type: pub fn on_trigger_hover_with<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: StateAccessor<V, PreviewCardState>, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the trigger's hover behavior against a per-instance state accessor.

entries.name: on_popup_hover
entries.type: pub fn on_popup_hover<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PreviewCardState, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's hover behavior, which keeps an open card open.

entries.name: on_popup_hover_with
entries.type: pub fn on_popup_hover_with<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: StateAccessor<V, PreviewCardState>, on_open_change: Change, ) -> HoverListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's hover behavior against a per-instance state accessor.

entries.name: on_dismiss
entries.type: pub fn on_dismiss<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PreviewCardState, on_open_change: Change, ) -> DismissListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's dismissal behavior for Escape and outside presses. Attach the returned handle with [`crate::Element::on_dismiss`].

entries.name: on_dismiss_with
entries.type: pub fn on_dismiss_with<V: 'static, Change>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, access: StateAccessor<V, PreviewCardState>, on_open_change: Change, ) -> DismissListener<V> where Change: Fn(&mut V, bool, &mut EventContext) + 'static,
entries.description: Build the popup's dismissal behavior against a per-instance state accessor.

entries.name: schedule
entries.type: pub fn schedule<V: 'static>(cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, state: &PreviewCardState)
entries.description: Ask for the one repaint an armed open or close deadline needs. Call this while rendering. A settled preview card requests nothing, so the window sleeps.

sections.name: PreviewCard::root_with
sections.signature: pub fn root_with(self, root: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the optional application-owned structural wrapper. A preview card needs no wrapper of its own; this part exists so a composition that wants one keeps the trigger out of the window's native drag region without inventing appearance.

sections.name: PreviewCard::root
sections.description: Create the unstyled root part. Use [`Self::root_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: PreviewCard::trigger_with
sections.signature: pub fn trigger_with(self, trigger: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned link-like trigger without adding appearance. Unlike a popover trigger, this projects the Link role: a preview card previews a destination rather than opening a menu, so the trigger stays an ordinary link for the keyboard and for assistive technology.

sections.name: PreviewCard::trigger
sections.description: Create the unstyled trigger part. Use [`Self::trigger_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: PreviewCard::portal_with
sections.signature: pub fn portal_with(self, portal: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned portal boundary. QuickGUI's retained overlay node is itself the portal, so this is the same boundary as [`Self::positioner_with`]; mount exactly one of them.

sections.name: PreviewCard::portal
sections.description: Create the unstyled portal part. Use [`Self::portal_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: PreviewCard::positioner_with
sections.signature: pub fn positioner_with(self, positioner: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the caller-owned positioner without adding appearance.

sections.name: PreviewCard::positioner
sections.description: Create the unstyled positioner part. Use [`Self::positioner_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: PreviewCard::popup_with
sections.signature: pub fn popup_with(self, popup: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned popup without adding layout or appearance. The popup emits [`crate::Event::Dismiss`] under [`Self::popup_id`] for Escape and for an outside pointer press, and restores focus to the trigger.

sections.name: PreviewCard::popup
sections.description: Create the unstyled popup part. Use [`Self::popup_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: PreviewCard::arrow_with
sections.signature: pub fn arrow_with(self, arrow: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate the application-owned arrow. The arrow is decorative: it carries a stable identity so the application can position and animate it, and is hidden from assistive technology.

sections.name: PreviewCard::arrow
sections.description: Create the unstyled arrow part. Use [`Self::arrow_with`] to supply an existing element.

sections.name: PreviewCard::backdrop_with
sections.signature: pub fn backdrop_with(self, backdrop: Element) -> Element
sections.description: Decorate an optional caller-painted viewport backdrop.

sections.name: PreviewCard::backdrop
sections.description: Create the unstyled backdrop part. Use [`Self::backdrop_with`] to supply an existing element.

typescript/ui/toast.example:
const toast = useToastManager();

toast.add({ id: "saved", title: "Saved", description: "Your changes are live." });

<Toast.Provider timeout={5000} limit={3}>
  <Toast.Portal>
    <Toast.Viewport toasts={toast.toasts()} onDismiss={toast.dismiss}>
      <For each={toast.toasts()}>{(item) =>
        <Toast.Root toastId={item.id}>
          <Toast.Content><Toast.Title /><Toast.Description /></Toast.Content>
          <Toast.Close><Text>Close</Text></Toast.Close>
        </Toast.Root>
      }</For>
    </Toast.Viewport>
  </Toast.Portal>
</Toast.Provider>

entries.name: orientation
entries.type: pub const fn orientation(mut self, orientation: MenuOrientation) -> Self
entries.description: Move the roving highlight along the other axis, Base UI's Root `orientation`. A horizontal menu installs [`POPOVER_MENU_HORIZONTAL_KEY_CONTEXT`] instead of [`POPOVER_MENU_KEY_CONTEXT`], so Left and Right move between top-level triggers and Down opens the highlighted submenu. Nothing else about the model changes.

entries.description: The item currently checked in one radio group, Base UI's `Menu.RadioGroup` `value`.

entries.name: set_radio_value
entries.type: pub fn set_radio_value( &mut self, group: impl Into<ElementId>, value: impl Into<ElementId>, ) -> bool
entries.description: Check exactly one item in a radio group, Base UI's `Menu.RadioGroup` `onValueChange`. Every other item in the group is unchecked in the same update, so a group can never retain two checked values. Returns whether anything changed; an item ID that is not a radio item in `group` changes nothing.

entries.description: Drop the highlight from `index` when the pointer leaves it, returning whether it changed. A native menu shows no highlighted row once the pointer has left the surface, so a row the pointer lit up goes dark when it leaves; a highlight the keyboard moved elsewhere in the meantime is left alone.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::element
sections.signature: pub fn element<V, Render, Dismiss>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PopoverMenu, root: Element, render_item: Render, dismiss: Dismiss, ) -> Element where V: 'static, Render: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element, Dismiss: Fn(&mut V, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer for one menu level. `render_item` owns all row geometry, colors, indicators, icons, and typography. Commands dispatch through the popover owner's ordinary typed-action path before `dismiss` runs.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::element_with_submenus
sections.signature: pub fn element_with_submenus<V, Render, Dismiss, OpenSubmenu>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PopoverMenu, root: Element, render_item: Render, dismiss: Dismiss, open_submenu: OpenSubmenu, ) -> Element where V: 'static, Render: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element, Dismiss: Fn(&mut V, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, OpenSubmenu: Fn(&mut V, ElementId, PopoverMenu, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer and expose submenu activation to the owner.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::element_with_submenus_and_hover
sections.signature: pub fn element_with_submenus_and_hover<V, Render, Dismiss, OpenSubmenu, HoverItem>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PopoverMenu, root: Element, render_item: Render, dismiss: Dismiss, open_submenu: OpenSubmenu, hover_item: HoverItem, ) -> Element where V: 'static, Render: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element, Dismiss: Fn(&mut V, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, OpenSubmenu: Fn(&mut V, ElementId, PopoverMenu, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, HoverItem: Fn(&mut V, usize, bool, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer with owner-controlled hover behavior. This is the native-overflow adapter hook for delayed submenu opening and menu-aim safe corridors. `hover_item` receives entry and exit transitions for enabled interactive rows; it owns highlighting and any delayed work. The ordinary [`Self::element_with_submenus`] method preserves immediate-highlight behavior without allocating a timer.

A horizontal menu installs [`POPOVER_MENU_HORIZONTAL_KEY_CONTEXT`] instead of [`POPOVER_MENU_KEY_CONTEXT`], so Left and Right move between top-level triggers and Down opens the highlighted submenu. Nothing else about the model changes.

entries.description: Check exactly one item in a radio group, Base UI's `Menu.RadioGroup` `onValueChange`. Every other item in the group is unchecked in the same update, so a group can never retain two checked values. Returns whether anything changed; an item ID that is not a radio item in `group` changes nothing.

sections.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer and expose submenu activation to the owner.

sections.name: PopoverMenu::element_with_submenus_and_hover
sections.signature: pub fn element_with_submenus_and_hover<V, Render, Dismiss, OpenSubmenu, HoverItem>( &self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut PopoverMenu, root: Element, render_item: Render, dismiss: Dismiss, open_submenu: OpenSubmenu, hover_item: HoverItem, ) -> Element where V: 'static, Render: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element, Dismiss: Fn(&mut V, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, OpenSubmenu: Fn(&mut V, ElementId, PopoverMenu, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static, HoverItem: Fn(&mut V, usize, bool, &mut EventContext) + Clone + 'static,
sections.description: Build the complete unstyled interaction layer with owner-controlled hover behavior. This is the native-overflow adapter hook for delayed submenu opening and menu-aim safe corridors. `hover_item` receives entry and exit transitions for enabled interactive rows; it owns highlighting and any delayed work. The ordinary [`Self::element_with_submenus`] method preserves immediate-highlight behavior without allocating a timer.

sections.description: Decorate an optional caller-painted backdrop, Base UI's `ContextMenu.Backdrop`. The native popover surface already takes the pointer grab, so this layer exists only for a caller-painted dimming pass inside the owner window. It is hidden from assistive technology and carries no appearance of its own. Mount it only while [`Self::is_open`] is true.

sections.name: ContextMenuState::element
sections.signature: pub fn element<V, BuildMenu, RenderRoot, RenderItem>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access: fn(&mut V) -> &mut ContextMenuState, target: Element, layout: ContextMenuLayout, build_menu: BuildMenu, render_root: RenderRoot, render_item: RenderItem, ) -> Element where V: 'static, BuildMenu: Fn(&mut V, &ContextMenuEvent) -> Option<PopoverMenu> + 'static, RenderRoot: Fn() -> Element + 'static, RenderItem: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element + 'static,
sections.description: Attach a complete cursor-point popover-menu interaction to a caller-owned target. `build_menu` runs only on a secondary click and may return `None` to suppress the popover. `render_root` and `render_item` own all appearance. The framework owns only bounded model behavior, structural geometry, point placement, separate-surface lifetime, keyboard focus, dismissal, submenu parenting, and exact native-close synchronization.

sections.name: ContextMenuState::element_with
sections.signature: pub fn element_with<V, BuildMenu, RenderRoot, RenderItem>( self, cx: &mut ViewContext<'_, V>, id: impl Into<ElementId>, access_source: StateAccessor<V, ContextMenuState>, target: Element, layout: ContextMenuLayout, build_menu: BuildMenu, render_root: RenderRoot, render_item: RenderItem, ) -> Element where V: 'static, BuildMenu: Fn(&mut V, &ContextMenuEvent) -> Option<PopoverMenu> + 'static, RenderRoot: Fn() -> Element + 'static, RenderItem: Fn(&PopoverMenuItem, PopoverMenuItemState) -> Element + 'static,
sections.description: Attach the cursor-point popover-menu interaction against a per-instance state accessor. A host that owns one [`ContextMenuState`] per declared target passes an accessor that captures which state this target opens into.

entries.name: render
entries.description: Native SwiftUI component used as the trigger. This follows Base UI's composition shape: Trigger supplies behavior and `render` replaces its default element. The rendered component's own press handler runs before Trigger's behavior.

entries.name: onPress
entries.description: Called after the rendered component's own press handler and before the popover opens.

typescript/swift-ui/popover.example:
<Popover
  isPresented={open()}
  onIsPresentedChange={setOpen}
  attachmentAnchor="bottom"
  arrowEdge="top"
>
  <Popover.Trigger render={<Button label="Open" />} />
  <Popover.Content>
    <QuickGUIHostView width={280} height={120}>
      <SettingsPanel />
    </QuickGUIHostView>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover>
